title: Sins on the Road of Bones
summary: The hierarchy of sins for Cappadocians on the Road of the Bones.

claims.text: At the gentlest end, showing fear of death or failing to study a death can prompt a Conviction roll for a high-rated follower.
Lower down come refusing a chance to kill, refusing to feed while hungry, frenzy and keeping insight from a fellow follower.
The worst failings are letting compassion decide, acting out of self-sacrifice, needlessly stopping a death and showing disgust at death.

title: Giovanni Lineage
summary: A 2-point Merit for the newly Embraced Giovanni.

claims.text: The clan has lately Embraced leading members of the Venetian Giovanni family, necromancer-merchants with insight into a craft that may become a true Discipline.
A character with this Merit may learn Necromancy as an extra clan Discipline but begins no lower than 11th generation.
Giovanni characters cannot take Prescience or Mad Visions; those traits are oddly missing among them.

title: Prescience and Horrific Appearance
summary: A Merit and a Flaw found among the Graverobbers.

claims.text: Prescience, a 3-point Merit, gives brief, dim glimpses of a fixed future, such as whether someone can be trusted, handled by the Storyteller; they are not possible futures but murky pieces of what will come.
Horrific Appearance, a 3-point Flaw, heightens the clan’s corpselike look: skin flakes away, flesh may rot off nose and ears, and a smell of the grave hangs about.
A Cappadocian with this Flaw has Appearance 0, which can never be raised.

title: Reaper’s Passing
summary: A sixth-level Mortis power that brings a mortal close to death.

claims.text: With a touch, a Blood Point and a Manipulation + Medicine roll against the target’s Willpower, the Cappadocian gives a living target a near-death crisis such as a seizure or loss of breath.
One success causes slight discomfort and five a massive heart attack that may leave lasting mental scars.
It does not touch vampires; on a botch the user is laid low for the scene by visions of a gruesome Final Death.

title: The Leper’s Gait
summary: A seventh-level Mortis power that rots a limb.

claims.text: The Cappadocian touches the target, spends a Willpower point and rolls Stamina + Medicine against the target’s Willpower, needing more successes than the target’s Stamina.
The chosen limb becomes useless at once and falls away after days equal to the target’s Stamina; used on a mortal’s head it kills.
On a vampire the effect ends at the next rising, though a vampire struck in the head cannot feed or use Disciplines until then; a botch strikes the user’s own limb.

title: The Illness Unveiled and Blessed Resilience
summary: Combination and high Fortitude powers of the clan.

claims.text: The Illness Unveiled, from Auspex 2 and Fortitude 7, works like Soulsight but reveals any disease the subject has and can cure it by lending some of the user’s Fortitude, limited by what the Cappadocian knows.
Blessed Resilience saves the vampire from Final Death automatically, drawing lost body parts back to crawl into place and healing to Mauled, as long as enough Willpower remains.
The price is one dot lost forever from every Attribute, and catastrophic harm such as a volcano still destroys the vampire; it costs 36 experience to learn.

title: Early Necromancy
summary: The young Discipline of the Giovanni.

claims.text: Necromancy has only just appeared, held by the Giovanni and a very few other Cappadocians, and is known only to the third level.
The Venetian merchants guard it closely, teaching only basics to some Cappadocian sires, and Storytellers are told not to give it to non-Giovanni characters.

title: The Tragedy Revealed
summary: The first level of early Necromancy.

claims.text: Holding the skull or brain of someone recently dead, the necromancer rolls Perception + Occult at difficulty 8, or 10 if the remains are more than a fortnight old.
Each success sharpens the vision, from a vague sense of the death at one to the cause, the killer and the scene in perfect detail at five; a botch gives false information.
It fails on anyone who had reached Golconda.

title: Call Forth the Host and Corporeal Home
summary: The second and third levels of early Necromancy.

claims.text: Summoning a spirit needs its name, a piece of its corpse and a fifteen-minute rite in silence; Golconda vampires and those who held True Faith in life cannot be called.
The roll is Charisma + Occult against the spirit’s Willpower, repeated whenever the spirit tries to slip free after a question; a botch brings a lying, malign spirit instead.

Corporeal Home binds a summoned spirit into a container such as a box or locket after eight hours of concentration and an Intelligence + Occult roll, holding it for a week, with each renewal harder by one.
